rationale: The left theorem: if a line is perpendicular to a plane, then lines parallel to it are also perpendicular to that plane. The right theorem (a property): if a line is perpendicular to two intersecting lines in a plane, then it is perpendicular to the plane itself. These are different, though related, theorems about perpendicularity of lines and planes. One is a consequence/property of the definition, the other is a criterion for perpendicularity.
